title: Openness of the flat locus (finite presentation)
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] and let $M$ be a finitely presented $S$-module, i.e. $M\cong\operatorname{coker}(S^{\oplus s}\to S^{\oplus t})$ for some $s,t\ge0$ and some $S$-linear map. For a prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset S$ let $M_{\mathfrak q}$ be the localization of $M$ at $S\setminus\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], an $R$-module via $\varphi$. Then the set $\{\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}S: M_{\mathfrak q}\text{ is a flat }R\text{-module}\}$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] is open in $\operatorname{Spec}S$ with its Zariski topology [def-weil-affine-spectrum] (the topology whose closed sets are the sets $V(J)=\{\mathfrak q:\mathfrak q\supseteq J\}$, $J\subseteq S$ an ideal).

proof.text: At a flat prime q, obtain a Noetherian finite-type model A -> B, N, together with the pushout to R -> S, the S-linear module base-change equivalence, and flatness of N at the contracted prime p.

Apply the existing Noetherian flat-locus neighborhood theorem to p. It produces g outside p with N localized at every prime avoiding g flat over A. The image of g in S avoids q by the definition of contraction.

For every prime r of S avoiding the image of g, its contraction to B avoids g. Apply the pointwise base-change lemma to its model localization, obtaining R-flatness of M_r. Thus the basic open of the image of g lies in the flat locus and contains q. Apply isOpen_iff_forall_mem_open and openness of basic opens.
